name: intraday_momentum_ema_cross_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: Intraday trends in liquid stocks exhibit serial correlation over 30-120 minute windows due to institutional block execution (TWAP/VWAP algos splitting large orders). Once a directional move begins, the algo flow sustains it. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders either trade too-short timeframes (scalping noise) or too-long (missing the intraday trend). Not arbitraged away because intraday trend-following has low win rate and high drawdown — psychologically hard to execute.
mechanism: When multiple timeframe trends align, the probability of continuation increases because institutional flows that established the trend are still active. Trend-following algorithms and discretionary traders pile on, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that lasts until liquidity on the opposing side overwhelms the directional flow.

filters.vix_filter: vix between 13-28 (too low = no range, too high = whipsaw)

weaknesses: EMA crossover is the most lagging entry possible. By the time 9/21 cross, the move is often 40-50% done. On short intraday moves, this leaves little room.
Whipsaw in rangebound markets destroys P&L. ADX filter helps but ADX itself lags — by the time ADX drops below 20, you've already taken 2-3 losses.
Win rate of ~38% means long losing streaks (5-8 consecutive losses). Psychologically brutal for discretionary override risk.
prior_art: Standard dual EMA crossover with ADX filter. Textbook trend-following adapted to intraday. See: Trading Evolved (Clenow), Following the Trend.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
